cases.excerpt: A total of 888 incident RCCs and 356 RCC deaths were identified.

comparison.excerpt: In models including adjustment for body mass index and energy intake, there was no higher risk of incident RCC associated with consumption of juices (HR per 100 g/day increment = 1.03; 95% CI, 0.97-1.09)

confidence_interval.excerpt: In models including adjustment for body mass index and energy intake, there was no higher risk of incident RCC associated with consumption of juices (HR per 100 g/day increment = 1.03; 95% CI, 0.97-1.09), total soft drinks (HR = 1.01; 95% CI, 0.98-1.05), sugar-sweetened soft drinks (HR = 0.99; 95% CI, 0.94-1.05), or artificially sweetened soft drinks (HR = 1.02; 95% CI, 0.96-1.08).

continent.excerpt: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)

design.excerpt: Cox regression yielded adjusted HRs and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for RCC incidence and mortality

effect_size.excerpt: In models including adjustment for body mass index and energy intake, there was no higher risk of incident RCC associated with consumption of juices (HR per 100 g/day increment = 1.03; 95% CI, 0.97-1.09), total soft drinks (HR = 1.01; 95% CI, 0.98-1.05), sugar-sweetened soft drinks (HR = 0.99; 95% CI, 0.94-1.05), or artificially sweetened soft drinks (HR = 1.02; 95% CI, 0.96-1.08).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: in relation to intakes of juices and total, sugar-sweetened, and artificially sweetened soft drinks

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 389,220 EPIC participants with median age of 52 years at recruitment (1991-2000) were included.

timing.excerpt: median age of 52 years at recruitment (1991-2000)
